COURSE INTRODUCTION : (COURSE - 1, BLOCK - 1)
This is the course in Education for the First Semester of Four Year UG Programme. The term
Education has a broader connotation. Education is a process of life long learning. The derivative
meaning of education comes from the Latin word Educare and Educere which stand for drawing
out or bringing up the innate capacities and potentialities of the human being. As a human being,
we have to know the basic meaning and value of education, because education is the bedrock of
the total growth and development of an individual and the country. Education develops the
dynamic personality of an individual. By taking this course, the learners can also understand the
importance of education, how education helps us to adjust with our community, society, nation or
the world at large and participate in the development of the society and our country.
BLOCK INTRODUCTION
In this course, the First Unit deals with the meaning and concept of education, which
contains the definitions, process, types, and scope of education. The Second Unit identifies and
determines the importance of various aims of education. The Third Unit explains the concept of
school and community relationship and its interdependence as well as functions of the school and
home. Besides these, it also presents a good description on educational heritage, its
compositeness and the transmission and advancement of educational heritage through
education. The Fourth Unit deals with the curriculum about its different types and also identifies
the defects and various principles of curriculum construction at the primary and secondary level ,
Fifth Unit explains the needs and importance of national integration and the Sixth Unit deals with
the needs and importance of international understanding and also presents the role of education
for promoting international understanding outside the nation. The Seventh Unit identifies the
needs of value education as well as various value-oriented activities.
While going through a unit, you will notice some along-side boxes, which have been included to
help you know some of the difficult, unseen terms. Some ACTIVITY (s) have been included to
help you apply your own thoughts. Again, we have included some relevant concepts in LET US
KNOW along with the text. And, at the end of each section, you will get CHECK YOUR
PROGRESS questions. These have been designed to self-check your progress of study. It will
be better if you solve the problems put in these boxes immediately after you go through the
sections of the units and then match your answers with ANSWERS TO CHECK YOUR
PPROGRESS given at the end of each unit.

Meaning and concept of Education
The field of education is very wide and elaborate. It is education
through which man develops his thinking and reasoning, problem solving
ability and creativity, intelligence and aptitude, positive sentiments and skills,
good values and attitudes. Education modifies the behaviour of an individual.
Human beings acquire and learn something everyday and every moment.
Thus, the entire life of man is nothing but a process of education. Therefore,
education is called a continuous process and it is concerned with man as
he lives and grows in an evergrowing society.
1.3 MEANING AND DEFINITIONS OF EDUCATION
In this section, we are going to discuss the term of education, its meaning

1.3.1 Meaning of Education
Education has a wide connotation. It promotes the harmonious

Education . Different thinkers, philosophers, psychologists,

to nourish. According to another view, education means leading out
the inborn qualities, talents, powers and virtues of the child because
the words E means out of and duco means I lead . So the natural
endowment with which an individual comes to the world should be
developed, the creative power should be expressed and impulses,
urges and needs should be satisfied.According to this view,
development of individuality has got more importance that is mainly
the individual latent abilities, interests and aptitudes. This view
emphasises the all round drawing out of the best in the child and less
on the development of social efficiency for better adjustment in society.
Education has a great importance in the all round development of the
child. The importance of education has always been realised by all

Broad or Wider Meaning of Education
In the broader sense, education is called a continuous process.
It begins at birth and continues throughout life. Education is a process
of development from infancy to maturity, from cradle to the grave.
Broader meaning of education has been defined by different thinkers
from different points of view. According to Drever, Education is a
process of controlling and modifying the behaviour of the young so as
to produce a recognised type of behaviour in the adult. On the other
hand, Hopkins opines that Education in its widest sense includes
everything that exerts a formative influence. Similarly, Edward Thring
elaborated his idea and said that Education is the transmission of
life, by the living, to the living . In this sense, the famous American
pragmatic philosopher John Dewey expressed that Life itself is
development and development itself is life . Education covers the entire
life of the child. It includes all the influences which act upon an individual
during his passage from the cradle to the grave. Education is everything
which influences human behaviour and personality. This kind of
experience comes through a number of agencies like Family, School,
Society etc. The wider meaning of edcation basically implies that:
it is a life long process of learning.
it covers all the experiences of life.
there is no fixed curriculum and methods
it is free from rigidity
it is a process of adjustment.

1.4 PROCESS OF EDUCATION
Although in a broad sense, education is a life-long and continuous
process, yet for convenience to understand the term, the educationists
have divided education into three processes, which are briefly discussed
below:

Bi-Polar Process of Education
Education is a two-way process. Sir John Adams has described the
process of education as a bi-polar process. Here, the personality of the
teacher influences the students in all aspects. The teacher and the student
being the two poles, the resultant process of their co-operative effort is
education. Teachers, impart education and students acquire education.
Without teachers, students cannot learn anything; on the other hand, if
there are no students in the classroom, whom would the teacher teach Bi-
polar process of education is not only conscious but also a deliberate one.
Tripolar Process of Education
Today, education is a three-way process. Education involves an
interaction among the educands (students), the educator and the social
environment. The teacher tries to develop the personality of the student in
the light of the needs of the society. Here, both the teacher and the taught
make efforts for achieving the purpose or destination in a conducive
environment.
Education a Dynamic Process
Education is a dynamic process and it helps the individual in their
progress. Education reconstructs a new and better social pattern according
to changing needs of time, place and society. Education in a sense is related
to time, place and social change. The process of education helps the
individual in their development as well as in the development of the society.

1.5 TYPES OF EDUCATION
After developing a fair understanding of the basic meaning and concept
of education, let us discuss the different types of education. The process of
education can generally be divided into three types as shown below:
TYPES OF EDUCATION
FORMAL INFORMAL NON-FORMAL
Let us have a look into these three types separately:
Formal Education :
Formal education is planned by men consciously and deliberately. It
implies modification of behaviour through an organised system of education
which is specifically established for the purpose. Formal education has a
particular goal. Here, students and teachers are engaged for a definite
purpose. The purpose or objective of formal education is pre-determined.
There are some rules, regulations and formalities. Formal education is
imparted in the educational institutions like Schools, Colleges and
Universities. After the completion of the course with the help of examination
and evaluation, the concerned authority confers a degree and certificate to
the individual. It should be pointed out that formal education is not merely

fire.This is called the education of life which one gets through the informal
experiences. Informal education is incidental education and it has no
predetermined plan. Informal education is that type of education which we
get by living with others in the society. Informal education takes place both
consciously and unconsciously. It has no systematic procedure. It is casual
and gained through daily experience, activity and work. This type of education
is not confined to a place and a fixed time schedule. Informal education
starts from birth and goes on till death. Informal education is not imparted
by any specialised agencies established for the purpose. Here, neither the
student nor the teacher is conscious of the process. There is no prescribed
course for learning, no fixed time table and no formal ways of education.To
be more precise, the main features of non-formal education are:
it is not pre-planned
it is incidental
it is life-long process
there is no fixed curriculum, no specific method of teaching.
there is no examination, no certificate, degree and diploma.

After getting a better understanding about formal and informal education,
we should also know how both the types can be differentiated.
There are some differences between formal education and informal

Formal education has formal means and ends but on the other hand

students, whereas in Informal education there are no teachers and
students.
In formal education, both the teachers and the students are conscious
about the process but in Informal education, neither the teacher nor the
student is conscious about the process.
Formal education has some prescribed course and fixed time table but
in Informal education, there is no prescribed course and fixed time table.
Formal education is imparted in institutions such as School, College
and University but for Informal education, there is no fixed place.
In Formal education, examinations are held and degrees or certificates
are awarded, but in Informal education, there is no examination system
nor the provision of certificates or degree.
Formal education starts and ends at a particular stage but Informal
education continues throughout life.
Formal education leads to mental strain on the part of the learner since
he has to make serious efforts to learn, but Informal education is natural
and it does not cause much strain for the learner.

Non-formal Education :
Non-formal education is a system of education which is given outside
the formal system. Non-formal education is mainly for the de-institutionalised
students willing to pursue education. Non-formal education is an alternative
system of education. This type of education has flexibility in content,
organisation, methods, duration, timing and place of education to suit the
different needs of various people.
According to Coombs and Ahmad , non-formal education is an
organised systematic educational activity carried outside the frame work of
the established formal system, whether operating separately or an important
feature of some broader activity that is intended to serve identifiable learning,
and learning objectives . Formal education is meant for a selected few of a
definite age group, but non-formal education is intended for all ages and
sections of the society. Non-formal education embraces all who aspire to
learn. It fulfils different objectives like imparting knowledge, developing different
skills and promoting value among the people. In non-formal education, there
is an element of consciousness. Non-formal education is meant for school
drop outs employed or working person, the house wives, retired person and
many others who are looking for information, knowledge or training without a
degree or diploma.Thus non-formal education basically includes:
Open learning
Postal tution
Open university
Correspondence course
Seminars, radio, television etc.

2.3 NECESSITY OF AIMS IN EDUCATION
Before discussing the aims of education, we should be aware of
the necessity of these aims. We know that education is a purposeful and
organized activity which deliberately tries to modify the behaviours of the
educand, with a specific aim in view. This is the criterion with which all
educational efforts are being judged. It is only after we have fixed our aim of
education for a particular stage, e.g.-primary, secondary, university, we can
devise methods, means and curriculum and utilize them for attaining the
desired goal. Again, among the different types of education such as,
humanistic, scientific, technical, art, commercial etc. each of them have
their own aims. But as a whole, the general goal of education can be
considered as man making . Determining the aims of education is necessary
for the following reasons:
As we have already stated, education is a planned and organized activity,
a definite aim of education gives us direction to act in a definite way.
According to John Dewey, acting with an aim is all one with acting
intelligently . This signifies that if there is an aim in view, we are aware
what we are doing and why we are doing it. In this way, we can save
our time and energy and the activity becomes meaningful.
Aims are necessary to assess the outcomes or results of the educative
activity. We can easily review the ways and means adopted for acquiring
the desired goal and can think of the possibilities for further improvement.

Aim is, thus, a yardstick by which we can measure the success and
failure of work done in school.
Clear determination of educational aim can only ensure development of

Aims are necessary for efficient school management also. It helps in

Finally, aims provide continuity and significance to education. We know

new dimension of knowledge, developing new capacities in the individual

that a scheme of education is ultimately to be valued by its success
in fostering the highest degree of individual excellence . Thus, individual
aim believes that the success of education depends on the
development of highest potentialities of the individual. Therefore,
maximum opportunities should be made available to each individual
for developing their physical, moral, intellectual and spiritual

2.4.2. Social Aim of Education
Now that we know what individual aim of education is, let us
discuss the social aim of education.
Social aim believes that the state or society is the supreme and
individuals exist only for the society. Individuals cannot develop in
isolation from the society. Therefore, education must always work for
the welfare and progress of the society. According to this aim, the
interest of the society is supreme and the position of an individual is
always subordinated to the society or state. The basic philosophy of
social aim is that society is the ultimate reality and the individual cannot
rise above the social entity.
John Dewey is the chief supporter of the social aim of education
and he has elaborately discussed the social aim of education in his
book Democracy in education . He broadly outlined the aim of
education as social efficiency , which implies civic efficiency or
education for citizenship . According to him, every state must design
education for social welfare and efficiency. A socially efficient individual
will be economically self sufficient and he will not be a parasite on
society but will contribute positively towards the progress of the society.
With the development of democratic ideals in the political world,
Dewey s concept of social efficiency as an educational aim has gained
wider support throughout the world.

Man cannot live without the society. He develops through social
contacts and therefore, he needs to be trained and developed

Social efficiency must be achieved by the positive use of individual
power and capacities in social occupations. Such a person is not
a burden on society but contributes to its development. He also
abides by moral and social standards of conduct.
Democratic society requires individuals who are physically fit,
intellectually bright, economically self sufficient and morally well
disciplined, who can contribute to social progress. It is believed
that this can be achieved through social aim of education.
Gandhiji, the father of basic education in India, has also

scheme of basic education with the objective of making man a
better citizen and moulding him in accordance with the needs

After developing a fair understanding regarding social aim of

Firstly, social aim of education may develop the sense of

Secondly, social aim in its extreme form can never be accepted
as it reduces the individual to a mere non-entity.
Thirdly, the extreme notion of all powerful state or society is
that it ignores legitimate needs, desires and interests of the individual
and suppresses his creative power.
Fourthly, the concept of social aim, if understood narrowly may
prove harmful for a democratic country like India. The political group
in power may interpret it in terms of its own ideology and education
may become an instrument of struggle for political power.

2.4.3 Synthesis of Individual and Social Aims
Probably an impression has developed in our mind that individual
and social aims are contradictory to each other. But practically, it is
not so. These two types of aims may be opposed to each other if
stressed in their extreme form. But if you cut off their sharp edges
they become complimentary and related to each other. Therefore, the
extreme form of either of the two should be avoided.
If we examine both the aims of education dispassionately, we
shall find that neither the individual nor the society can exist without
each other. The individual is a product of society, while society finds
its advancement in the development of each individual member. In the
words of Sir John Adams, Individuality requires a social medium to
grow; without social contacts we are not human .

should be allowed to develop for the good of the society. Percy Nunn,
the main advocate of individual aim also believes in the need of social

Don t we think that syntheses of these two aims will be the ideal

In this connection, what is the function of a school The school should

should not go beyond this or should not curb the freedom of the
individual. On the other hand, the state should do everything possible
to promote happiness and welfare of each member of the society and
the individual too should work for progress and development of the
society.

2.4.4 Liberal Aim of Education
Now, we have a clear concept about Individual and Social aim
of education. Besides these two aims, there are some other specific
aims also. One such aim is liberal or knowledge aim of education. Let
us discuss what liberal aim is.
The concept of liberal aim of education is very old. Education in
the ancient times, whether in India or elsewhere mostly, emphasized
mostly the development of intellectual powers or knowledge. All learning
was for the sake of learning and scholarship. The function of the
Gurukula in India and the school in the west was to enable the child to
develop physically and mentally and to obtain all experiences
necessary for being a cultured individual in the society. As the aim of
education was to liberate the mind, provisions were made for subjects
like philosophy, logic, geometry, fine arts etc. in their curriculum.
The supporters of the liberal aim believe that man is considered
to be far superior to animals because of his certain cognitive abilities,

satisfaction. The present civilization has come to pass through the
dissemination of knowledge through the medium of education.
Socrates, the great Greek philosopher, also said that One who had

2.4.5. Vocational Aim of Education
Now we have understood the liberal aim of education. While
criticizing the liberal aim, we have opined that liberal education should
be provided with practical knowledge, for true development of the
individual. Vocational aim of education has laid stress on practical
aspects of education. To be more specific, it has given importance on
training in some vocation or craft, so that a person can earn his own
living in future life. This aim of education is gaining more and more
popularity with the advancement of science and technology and
changing socio-economic structure of the world. Vocationalisation is
an important slogan of modern democratic education and it is believed
that without a proper emphasis on vocational aspect of education,
those who merely go to school suffer all their lives.
We must understand the points, why vocational aim of education
is getting importance in the present times.
Vocational education makes one economically self sufficient.
Self sufficiency is a great source of satisfaction and strength.
Economic self sufficiency is the first characteristic of social
efficiency.
Vocational education strikes a balance between economic and
individual progress. It prepares students for a useful life and
useful occupation. In the words of Gandhiji, True education ought
to be a kind of insurance against unemployment .
Vocational aim of education reduces the impact of verbalism
and mere intellectual domination. Modern educationists have
supported the idea of vocational education. Rousseau and
Gandhiji were great supporters of this aim of education. Gandhiji
introduced craft centred education as a part of his basic
education scheme.
Vocational aim gives purpose to educational activity. It is based
on the simple principle of psychology that a child learns more
efficiently when he is engaged in purposeful activity which appeals
to his instincts and interests, stimulates his observations and

arouses his thoughts and feelings. Therefore, the Indian Education
Commission of 1964-66 has recommended the inclusion of work
experience in the secondary school curriculum.
Children having lower intelligence can be benefited by vocational
education. Such children are at great disadvantage when taught
academic subjects. Vocational training can help them towards
being self sufficient and thereby they can lead a respectful adult
life.
Vocational education is essential to bridge the gap between the
upper and lower classes of the society. In India, the education of
the upper classes has been purely literary till recent years and
vocational education was meant for the poor and laboring class.
Gandhiji who proved through experimentation that vocational
education has rich potentialities for intellectual development, if
performed intelligently said that it ultimately leads to harmonious
development of body, mind and soul.
Finally, vocational education develops the concept of dignity of
labour among the students. Every work whether big or small,
has its own importance.
Now let us discuss the grounds on which vocational aim of

Firstly, educationists have termed vocational aim as a narrow
aim of education on the ground that it has given importance on mere
earning of one s livelihood and that has reduced it to just bread and
butter aim.
Secondly, earning of livelihood is no doubt, a very important part
of human endeavour, but that is not all. Man has to develop physically,
mentally, morally and spiritually. If education is reduced to mere
vocational training alone, it will remain halfway for complete living.
Thirdly, purely vocational education will make our outlook narrow.
It may produce good mechanics, electricians, doctors and engineers
but not good human beings.

2.4.6 Harmonious Development Aim
Now we will discuss Harmonious development as an aim of
education. We have to understand the concept and the basic features
of this aim of education. First, we must have to know what harmonious
development in education means.
Harmonious development means developing the psycho-
physical and moral qualities of an individual in a balanced and
harmonious way. We know that a child inherits the faculties of body,
mind, and soul. Education should establish a harmony between these
aspects of development for emergence of an ideal personality.
Mahatma Gandhi also lays emphasis on harmonious development
when he says by education, I mean all-round drawing out of the best
in child and man -body, mind and spirit .
Pestalozzi was also a great supporter of the harmonious
development aim. He says The sole aim of education is the
harmonious development of the faculties and disposition which make
up personality .
Thus, this aim of education believes in the development of all
innate powers and capabilities of the child in a harmonious way in
order to produce a well balanced personality.

The Gurukula system: In this system, students stay with their
Guru at the Gurugriha away from home. The Guru used to give
liberal education based on spiritualism and religion. The students
were to live and do everything under the supervision of the Guru.
Monastery: Buddhist education was centered round a monastery.
There were some private teachers who took ten to fifteen children
taught them in their houses. The rise of educational institutions
may be attributed to the influence of Buddhism. The monasteries
may be called the counterparts of Gurukulas. The monastery or

the Mosque as a part of religious activity. The religious chief
known as Maulabi used to take charge of education as his
religious responsibility. It functioned as a primary educational
institution in Muslim period. Along with letters numbers, the
principles of Quran, Gulistan Bastan, Chikandarnama etc. were

Lower Madrassa and Higher Madrassa: These were Islamic

respectively. The subjects like Grammar, Literature, Persian,
Arabic, Geometry, Economics and History were taught at the

Arithmetic, Advance Geometry, Sciences, Medicine and
Engineering etc. were taught in the Higher Madrassa. These
institutions were financed by the Government or the rich people.
Higher Madrassa was located in the bigger towns.
Pathsala: It was a popular institution of learning at the lower
level specifically for Hindu children as a counterpart of the
Madrassa. Subjects like language study, grammar, arithmetic,
accountancy social studies, moral lessons etc. were taught in
these institutions. The method of teaching was verbal.

important component of education, that is curriculum and its meaning, types,

4.3 CONCEPT AND MEANING OF CURRICULUM
We are all familiar with the term of curriculum. Curriculum is an
essential tool for running the programme of educational instruction in the
formal schooling. Each and every educational institution has some planned
activities and programmes in the name of curriculum and co-curricular
activites which are meaningful and significant for the students in their real
life. Because through the various skillful and value-oriented curricular and
co-curricular activities students can develop their physical, emotional and
intellectual capacities that lead to their all round development. In order to
have some clarity about its basic meaning, we have to know the origin of
the term curriculum. The term curriculum is derived from Latin word
Currere which means run . The very meaning of curriculum means a course
to be run for reaching a certain goal or destination. Thus, in an educational
institution, education is imagined as a race, with its aim as the goal and
curriculum as the course leading to that goal.
In a more precise term, we can define curriculum in the words of an
educationist, Cunningham as a tool in the hands of artist (teacher) to mould
his material (pupils) according to his ideals (aims and objectives) in his
studio (school) This definition explains that curriculum is a course of study,
designed to be followed at the various levels of education.
In the opinion of Crow and Crow (as quoted in the book Safaya, R.N.
and Shaida, B.D. (1996): Development of Educational Theory and
Practice ) Curriculum includes all the learner s experiences in or outside
the school that are included in a programme which has been devised to
help his development, physically, emotionally, socially, spiritually and
morally. Here the main logic of curriculum is to develop the total learning
experiences of the students in their life.

4.5 DEFECTS OF CURRICULUM
In this section, we will discuss briefly the various defects of
curriculum for a better understanding as to what type of curriculum is
prevalent in our present teaching-learning process and what are the
drawbacks due to which the students are unable to have good learning
experiences that can help them to reach a certain goal in their life. The
basic defects of curriculum are found by Secondary Education Commission
after a thorough analysis of curriculum. Let us discuss the following defects-
Rigid and Static: In formal schooling, the curriculum is pre-designed and
pre-determined for teaching-learning process. The curriculum is based
on subject instruction. The main emphasis is given on bookish knowledge;
importance is given on what teachers want, not on what students desire.
Narrowly conceived: The present curriculum is rather degree oriented
and meets the requirements for passing the school stages.
Emphasis of Bookish knowledge: The present curriculum prevalent in
our education system mostly gives emphasis on the theoretical and
academic side, rather than practical one.
Single Track curriculum: The curriculum lacks adequate provisions for
the diversity of tastes and talents.
Absence of Technical and Vocational studies: In a democratic country
like ours, we have the need of more skilled persons (that is technically
fit) as well as more entrepreneurship facilities and trainings. Proper and
up to date education should provide such type of vocational and skillful
training that prepares the students for their future. But in formal schooling,
more importance is given on bookish knowledge rather than on practical
and vocational aspects. Besides these, there is also a lack of flexibility
which is needed to keep pace with a fast changing world.
Domination by Examination: The curriculum is dominated by
examination. It concentrates more on enabling the students to pass
examinations and not to acquire knowledge in a wider manner. Because
it is time bound, the contents of the topics and the types of the study are
determined by the questions to be asked in the examinations.

BASIC PRINCIPLES OF CURRICULUM
CONSTRUCTION AT PRIMARY AND
SECONDARY LEVEL
For constructing a curriculum, some principles should be followed in
order to cater to the needs and interests of the students from the school to
college and university levels. But it is required to see their interests and needs
separately. Besides, the mental level of the students should also be taken in
to account. Now let us discuss the basic principles, which should be followed
while constructing a curriculum at the primary and secondary level.
The principles which should be followed at Primary level:
Curriculum should be child centred: Curriculum should be based on the
present needs and circumstances of the children. At the time of curriculum
construction, mental level of the students should be considered.
Curriculum should provide a fullness of experience for children: Curriculum
should be constructed not only to include some certain academic subjects
like sciences, mathematics, work experiences, languages, art and music,
health and physical education, the knowledge of which is very vital for the
learners; but it should also have enough space for some other activities
like drama, excursion, regional study, laboratory work, drawing, original
composition, collection for museum etc. It may also include some other
co-curricular activities like games, social service, scouting and guiding,
N.C.C. etc. These activities should form a regular feature of the normal
working of the institution in order to empower the students with experiences
that would help them to reach their ideals in life.
Curriculum should be Community centred: The main purpose of the
curriculum is to serve the children s needs and to enable them to adjust
themselves in society. Actually, the very meaning of the school is to
serve the needs and demands of the society where it is established. In
fact, it is the school which the students attend as members of the society.
Curriculum, therefore, should be prepared keeping in view the needs
and changing nature of the society.
Curriculum should be integrated: Curriculum should follow the principle
of integration through which to bring about integration between children s

needs and activities with the needs of a democratic society, where the
main focus is on technological as well as innovative ideas and
pedagogical knowledge.
Curriculum should be Activity centred: While catering for the children s
interest, curriculum should be centered round the multipurpose activities
to ensure the development of Hand, Heart and Head of the children
through the process of Learning by doing System.
Creative Principle: Curriculum should include such subjects through
which creative power of the children can be encouraged and chalked
out. In preferring the subjects for teaching-learning process, the students
interest must be primary focus so that their creativity can be encouraged.
The principle of Elasticity and variety: Curriculum should be flexible in
nature, because a rigid and static curriculum can not meet the
requirement of the children. Therefore, the curriculum should be elastic
and broad based to corporate with the new subjects and activities as
demanded by the changing times. In fact, curriculum should be based
on student s consideration and their requirements.
The principle of comprehensiveness: Curriculum should follow the
principle of comprehensiveness including all the necessary facts or
details about requirement of the students and their interest. The
curriculum must be comprehensive enough to generate the needs of
various individuals and communities with keeping the needs of various
types of pupils.
The Principle of Balanced: Curriculum should maintain a balance
between the theoretical and practical subjects for developing the
potentialities or capabilities of the students in order by enabling them to
face and perform in any kind of competitive situation of the society.
Balanced curriculum should include individual and social aims of
education, professional and liberal education, compulsory and elective
subjects of education in accordance with the mental level of the students.

Totality of Experience: This principle believes that curriculum should
not only include the academic subjects but also the whole ranges of
experiences that the student faces both inside and outside the school. It
is the curriculum from which students get experiences like class room,
library, laboratory, workshop, playgrounds besides numerous formal and

5.3 MEANING OF NATIONAL INTEGRATION
We use the term Integration to mean the combination of different
parts into a whole. But what is the actual meaning of National Integration
National Integration is much more than a combination or unity among its
members. It includes the feelings and sentiments of its citizens which govern
their political and public behaviour. National Integration is the feeling of
oneness where all its citizens are integrated through sharing with one
another, their joys, sorrows, smiles, tears and a common interest in the
welfare of the nation as a whole. The citizens of an integrated nation have
mutual understanding, tolerance and respect for the culture, traditions and
ways of life of the different sections of people of their country. They have
common national ideals, common objectives, common interests and above
all, a profound confidence in the future of the nation. Are we not worried,
when a member of our family is sick Yes, because we are concerned
about one another s welfare and problems and, above all, we are emotionally
attached to each other despite external differences. So, in short, it is the
National Integration which keeps members of a nation united through the
sharing of an emotional attachment. It is through Emotional Integration only
that National Integration can be achieved.
In the words of Humayun Kabir, National Integration does not depend
on race or language or religion or geography, singly or collectively, though
they help, but on the feeling of belonging to one nation
According to Pandit Nehru, Let us, the citizens of the Republic of
India stand up with straight backs and look up at the skies, keeping our feet
firmly planted on the ground and bring about this synthesis, this integration
of the Indian people. Political integration has already taken place, but what
I am after is something deeper than that, an emotional integration of the
Indian people so that we may be welded into one strong national unit,
maintaining at the same time all our wonderful diversity.

5.3.2 Obstacles to National Integration
Till now, we have discussed the meaning as well as needs of
National Integration. But still, we have seen that there is a visible
lack of the feeling of oneness, unity and fellow feeling among us.
Why Don t you want to find out the causes Yes, we have answers
to these questions. Even after different endeavors from various
sources to unite our nation, we have failed to achieve this objective.
So, let us look in to the following obstacles or hurdles which stand
in the way of National Integration
Communalism: The greatest menace to the national solidarity of a
country is communalism. There are many communities in India.
The problem of Communalism in India is an old problem. The British
by their policy of DIVIDE RULE caused the problem to grow
leading to the partition of the country. Communalism has been
identified as one of the main obstacles in the way of National
Integration.
Casteism: In the achievement of unity of the country, casteism
causes bitterness among the people. The different castes look only
at the benefit of their own castes. They do not bother for national
benefit. This system widens the gulf between the people of different
castes and prevents them from getting closer to one another. The
accident of birth confers a caste identity on them. That is how
casteism grows which hampers the spirit of integration.
Religious Prejudices: Religious prejudices are related to
communalism and casteism. Religious prejudice and communal
narrow-mindedness have caused the partition of our country and
they are still prevalent in one shape or the other. The different
ideologies of different religions sometimes inspire the followers to
translate these differences into action and enmity among them is
created.
Different Culture: Some people say that in India, as there are
different cultures so there are no chances of achieving unity. They

Provincialism: Another danger to national integration is

Economic Condition: Economic factors are also responsible for
the absence of a sound feeling of nationalism. The gap between the
rich and the poor class, the peasant and the big land holders, the
industrialist and the workers is increasing. Lack of employment

youth, who take to violence and even to anti-social and anti-national
activities, affecting the integration of the nation.
Social Differences: In India, social conditions of the people have

7.3 MEANING OF VALUE EDUCATION
Before defining the meaning and concept of value education, let us
discuss the meaning of value.
Generally speaking, values are the norms of behaviour which have
been evolved during the course of time in the social, moral and spiritual
fields. It refers to the ideals in various acts of behaviour. In other words,
value stands for the ideals of a man/woman that he/she lives for.
Philosophically speaking, a human being is supposed to conduct
himself and shape his/her life patterns by integrating his beliefs, ideas and
attitudes. Values are those standards or code of moral behavior conditioned
by one s cultural tenets and guided by his/her conscience. Thus, good of all
qualities can be taken as the sole criterion for values.
From psychological point of view, value is associated with the feeling
aspect of behavior. It means that receiving knowledge about the value is not
enough; it is necessary that it must be integrated into the personality of an
individual so that it may be characterized. Thus as the individual grows, he/
she learns from his/her experiences, which may come as general guides to
behaviour. These guides which tend to give direction to life, may be called
values .
From the above discussion, it is clear that an individual s personality
is determined by a set of values that he/she adopts as personal preferences
of ideals. Thus, value does not exist as objects but is estabilished by
judgements that is, by judging things, qualities, events or actions from a
personal point of view. Values are subjective in the sense that they exist
only for those who uphold them. But it contains objective element also
because different thinkers perceive values in various perspectives according
to their thinking. Allport define, value as a belief upon which a man acts by
preference. In the words of eminent sociologist R K Mukherjee, values are
socially approved desires and goals that get internalized through the process

7.5 VALUE EDUCATION, ITS NEED AND IMPORTANCE
Already we have discussed the different aspects of value. Now the
question is, why are we giving importance to value education Why is it
necessary to provide value education at all levels of education We will try
to analyse these aspects in this section of the unit.
Our society has seen the erosion of social and moral values in the
younger generation which has given rise to serious social and ethical conflicts
in society. To counter the erosion of values, a positive intervention is the
only way. Value education has become extremely necessary in the context
of today. Rapid scientific growth and technological development or
advancement resulting in industrialization have threatened age old moral
standards. The National Policy on Education of 1986 has laid considerable
emphasis on value education by highlighting the need to make education a
purposeful and powerful tool for cultivation of social and moral values. It
states: In our culturally plural society, education should foster universal
and eternal values oriented towards the unity and integration of our people.
Value education has a profound positive content based on our heritage,
national goals and universal perceptions. In the context of social changes,
education is not only to impart information and to teach skills to the students
but also to inculcate the values of humanism, democracy, socialism,
secularism and national integration. A large number of educationists of the
whole world have stressed the importance of promoting values through

education, which is facing the crisis of character in different spheres of life.
University Education Commission of 1949 held the view that in addition to
the search for truth through scientific and scholarly pursuits, an important
task of education is a concern with values. National Education Commission
of 1964-66 with emphasis on education s role in national development
includes among the functions of higher education, cultivation of right interests,
attitudes and moral and intellectual values. In 1986 National Policy on
Education observes that the growing concern over the erosion of essential
values and an increasing cynicism in society has brought to focus the need
for readjustments in the curriculum in order to make education as a forceful
tool for the cultivation of social and moral values. The programme of Action
(POA) suggests a workable line of action to achieve an interlinking of
education and culture in order to promote the process of child s personality
development, particularly in terms of discovering the inherent potentialities
of all the children. Thus, value oriented education is the need of the time
and it is justified on the following grounds:
Development of positive social attitudes: Valuables based
education will help in developing positive social attitudes. Through value
based education, the students will be aware of many evils of the society,
such as, corruption, nepotism, favoritism, riots, merciless killing of the
innocents, dowry etc. which are hampering the progress of the nation.
They will be able to realize their voice against these evils.
Development of moral qualities: Value based education is needed
for developing moral qualities among the students. Qualities like
truthfulness, honesty, respect for elders, spirit of service, tolerance,
sympathy, sacrifices are the basis of character and personality
development. Value based education will help in developing these
qualities.
Counters materialistic attitudes: Modern world is in the grip of
materialistic values like money, property, land or other kind of wealth
etc. Value education is an effective tool to fight against materialistic
attitudes. It creates respect for moral or human values without which
one can not lead a good life.

Humanizing effect: Value based education aims at humanizing or

Development of democratic qualities: For developing democratic
